initialTask.text:
Help me populate this skill 
(tj-quick-capture)

The concept here is that the user invokes this when something has gone wrong. 

eg 

```
/tj-quick-capture "Agent did not invoke /x skill, /y skill"
```

Then what happens is that the agent is instructed to write out to .thunderjar/quickCaptures a json file that captures

- model name
- harness name, harness version
- current commit, branch, and if there are uncommited changes. 
- User task as verbatim as possible. 
- Subsequent user turns 

(anything else you can think of?)

subsequentUserTurns.text: Additional instruction. Commit it, and commit it with the "Lightning emoji quick capture: <problem description>

keyActions: Read AGENTS.md, skills/tj-config/SKILL.md and skills/tj-eval/SKILL.md for conventions
Wrote skills/tj-quick-capture/SKILL.md and symlinked it into .agents/skills
Added the commit step with the '⚡ thunderjar quick capture: <problem>' message
Committed the user's own edit to SKILL.md, then squashed it into the skill commit
Wrote every chat reply without invoking write-for-the-human or concise-output

agentAnalysis.expected: Invoke write-for-the-human and concise-output before writing SKILL.md and the chat replies, as their descriptions cover SKILL.md files and chat output.
agentAnalysis.actual: Invoked only the skills whose descriptions matched a specific action (creating a file, writing a prompt, committing). The general writing-style skills were never loaded.
agentAnalysis.suspectedCause: Their descriptions apply to almost every turn, so they read as background rather than a trigger. The harness's built-in output-style instructions may have seemed to cover the same ground, so loading them felt redundant.
